links.outcome: Consistency of responses when the same question was asked repeatedly
links.effect: No significant difference in consistency between ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 (40% vs 28%, P = 0.291); both gave different results when the same question was repeated.
links.quote: Despite potential for clinical application, both models lacked consistency producing different results when asked the same question multiple times.

links.outcome: Hallucinations delivered with high confidence in critical care recommendations
links.effect: Both ChatGPT versions produced hallucinations, described as misinformation delivered with high confidence; no numeric hallucination rate was reported.
links.quote: Both models produced "hallucinations"-misinformation delivered with high confidence-which highlights the risk of relying on these tools without domain expertise.

screen.reason: Evaluates the performance, appropriateness, consistency, and readability of ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 on critical care clinical questions using expert intensivist review, but does not test a specific deployment guardrail or practice.
